notes.what: GH #421 tower training-step profile close-out: pre-registered (contract v2.5, frozen 2026-09-07 before measurement) census of the CLIP-text, OpenCLIP-vision and HTSAT LoRA training steps. Decides the candidate ports the contract names (C-ATTN-CLIP-text, C-ATTN-CLIP-vision, C-MLP-CLIP-text, C-MLP-CLIP-vision) and reports the already-realized fused-kernel gains (C-LORA, C-LN, C-GELU-HTSAT joint) plus the out-of-tier, named-but-undecided C-ATTN-HTSAT chain.
notes.nsys: Nsight Systems 2025.3.2.474 (dnf-installed from the cuda-rhel8 repo; the pod image's own cuda-12.6 shim and an unpinned 2026.1.3 build were both refused by the job script)
recorded_deviations: run1 (pod p421, session 1) was ALL-12-LEGS INVALID at the pre-fix tip (esc-088: profile_421_legs.sh's corpus tuple shared stdout with its own producers, fixed by PR #469, main c1b0b0ba) -- this artifact is the full 12-leg re-run (run2) on the merged fix.

ROOT CAUSE of the run2-pass1..3 'A2 legs INVALID for attribution -> F32-only' state (pass-4 item 1, kernel_census.py): the module keyed each GPU-kernel bucket on shortName alone, and cutlass's Kernel2<...> template wrapper (same latent shape in magma_sgemmEx_kernel<...>) gives every bf16 GEMM tile instantiation the SAME literal shortName -- clip-text-A2's own run_m.sqlite has 3 DISTINCT cutlass instantiations sharing shortName='Kernel2' AND grid/block, so keying on shortName summed them into one anonymous row that tripped profile_421_attribute.py's 1% known-kernel-name gate. FIX: key on COALESCE(demangledName, shortName) instead -- a strict refinement (a bucket can only split, never merge two old buckets into fewer new ones), so gpu_kernel_us_per_step stays bit-identical and only by_kernel_and_grid resplits; only the cutlass Kernel2<...>(T1::Params) wrapper is stripped to its inner tile name, every other demangled name (magma's own template signature, splitKreduce_kernel<...>) is kept as-is since its template arguments are what distinguishes real instantiations there. All 12 censuses were regenerated under the fix for this run2 pass-4 pull -- every top-line number (gpu_kernel_us_per_step, wall/front/busy per_step) is UNCHANGED (sum-preserving refinement); only the per-instantiation by_kernel_and_grid breakdown resplit. Both CLIP-tower A2 legs (clip-text-A2, clip-vision-A2) are now VALID and decision-grade for attribution -- every candidate-port decision below is measured on BOTH the F32 (A1) and BF16 (A2) legs, never F32-only by consequence.

htsat-A2 (bf16) is VALID at the merge level but NOT decision-grade for attribution: UNATTRIBUTED share_gpu_busy is 5.66%, over the contract's 5% validity bound. Root cause: WINDOWING (window-partition/reverse/roll copies) and FRONT-FUSION (the audio front end's own activation) are still UNDECLARED chains -- a window-partition copy sits at the identical element count as a generic residual-stream PERMUTE/RESHAPE copy, so profile_421_attribute.py has no shape-only way to tell them apart, and declares neither rather than guess (module doc, 'declaring a chain with no matching rule is dishonest'). htsat-A1 (f32) clears the bound under the pass-4 census fix and IS decision-grade. HTSAT has no candidate port under this contract in the first place (C-ATTN-HTSAT is a named, measured, declared-out-of-tier chain, never folded into UNATTRIBUTED), so htsat-A2's own non-decision-grade status never blocks a candidate-port decision.

Per-leg raw .nsys-rep exports were deleted on-pod after each leg's census.json was produced (disk budget); the raw sqlite exports (24 files) were kept off-pod and were never committed -- see notes.operator_recorded for the on-pod-recorded total size, which has no in-tree witness.

Both media corpus producers (image, audio) emit families x instances = 24 files at any --rows, so the M-leg's 4800 rows cycle 16 distinct train clips (a page-cached working set, contract SS D6.3) -- the HTSAT/vision front-end finding below is a real per-item CPU decode/preprocess compute cost, not a realistic-corpus I/O cost, and every quote of that finding must carry this caveat.

Census reports produced before the pass-4 kernel-identity fix (the #356 close-out and the #421 2026-09-01/06 pod artifacts) carry the pre-fix, collapsed Kernel2/magma_sgemmEx_kernel rows in by_kernel_and_grid -- their by_kernel_name totals and every other top-line number are unaffected (the refinement is sum-preserving, see the root-cause deviation above), only the per-instantiation breakdown was coarser.

CONTRACT.md's own SS D5 (docs/plans/66-tower-profile/CONTRACT.md, frozen body) names profile_421_merge.py's hermetic suite at a fixed pre-registration-time count -- already stale at the freeze commit (perf/421-profile-p1 @ aace002f), where the live suite (unittest discovery over the REAL committed test_profile_421_merge.py, never hand-typed -- see profile_421_artifact.py's compute_merge_suite_test_count) already carried 55 tests; unchanged at c1b0b0ba. Not corrected in the frozen body -- a pre-registration's text is never edited after freezing -- recorded here instead, per docs/plans/66-tower-profile/README.md's own 'Deviations from a clean single pass' section (see CONTRACT.md SS D5 itself, never quoted here as a second, independently-drifting digit, for the exact stale figure it names). The count is descriptive prose about the suite's size, not a method parameter any decision rule reads, so this staleness never affected a verdict.

operator_recorded.raw_sqlite_export_total_size: ~31 GB (on-pod estimate at run2 close-out, before the exports were deleted per the disk-budget deviation above; the raw .sqlite files themselves were never committed, so no in-tree witness can re-derive this figure -- the file COUNT in notes.recorded_deviations IS witnessed, this size is not)

findings.text: The HTSAT training step is CPU front-end-bound: front-end share of wall is 81-83% across the F32/BF16 decision legs (rule: front_share_of_wall >= 50% on every leg read; audio decode/resample/STFT/mel dominating wall time). Front-end time itself is 1.249-1.255 s/step across every F32/BF16 x A/D-arm leg read (relative spread 0.5%, within the 5% arm-invariance rule), so this cost is dtype- and arm-invariant.

evidence.arm_invariance_rule: (max-min)/mean of front_s_per_step across every A/D leg read <= 0.05

findings.text: CLIP-vision's image decode/preprocess front end is 20-22% of wall on the F32/BF16 decision legs.

At batch 8 the CLIP training steps are launch-bound: 3638-3722 launches/step across the four F32/BF16 A-arm CLIP legs (text and vision) (rule: launches/step >= 1000 and launch/sync residual share of wall (residual_s_per_step / wall_s_per_step) >= 20%, both on every named leg); switching to BF16 cuts GPU busy by 32-41% per tower while wall drops by only 4-5%.

evidence.launch_bound_rule: launches/step >= 1000 and launch/sync residual share of wall (residual_s_per_step / wall_s_per_step) >= 20%, both on every named leg

findings.text: C-ATTN-HTSAT is measured, not a candidate port: 33% of GPU busy (~5% of wall) on the F32 decision leg (htsat-A1). HTSAT attention (head_dim 24 at every stage) sits OUTSIDE the fixed-head-dim port tier by the contract's own declaration — this stays a measured, OPEN number, never folded into UNATTRIBUTED and never decided under this issue.
